---
title: "Female Baby Name Trends Since 2000"
format: html
execute:
  echo: true
  message: false
  warning: false
---

We compare the popularity trajectories of nine female baby names (**Alexa**, **Anna**, **Arriah**, **Jada**, **Janiah**, **Leah**, **Maddie**, **Marissa**, and **Sania**) from 2000 to 2025 using Social Security Administration data. Because some names have thousands of births per year while others are rarer, each panel uses its own vertical scale to highlight when each name peaked.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Read the combined SSA baby names dataset
baby_names <- read_csv("ssa-baby-names.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Target names to compare
selected_names <- c(
  "Alexa", "Leah", "Arriah", "Anna", "Marissa",
  "Sania", "Jada", "Maddie", "Janiah"
)

# Filter to female births from 2000 onward for our nine names
friends_names <- baby_names |>
  filter(
    sex == "F",
    year >= 2000,
    name %in% selected_names
  )

# Find each name's peak year since 2000 to highlight on the plot
peak_years <- friends_names |>
  slice_max(count, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = name)

# Plot a 3x3 grid of trends with shaded area and peak year dot
ggplot(friends_names, aes(x = year, y = count, color = name, fill = name)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.25, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = peak_years, size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Rise and Fall of Nine Female Names (2000–2025)",
    subtitle = "Dots mark each name's peak year since 2000 (note separate y-axis scales)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Babies Named per Year",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Social Security Administration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
